entry.note: the nested route upload_route (registered with @app.post on /_nicegui/client/{client_id}/upload/{element_id}) reads the multipart form via request.form() and passes each Starlette UploadFile, whose .filename is the client-supplied multipart filename, to create_file_upload; the resulting FileUpload list goes to Upload.handle_uploads, which wraps each file in UploadEventArguments(file=...) and dispatches it to every on_upload handler through events.handle_event

guards.note: clean: filename = PurePosixPath(upload.filename or '').name, which drops every '/'-separated directory component (so '../x' -> 'x', '/abs/x' -> 'x') before it becomes FileUpload.name of SmallFileUpload/LargeFileUpload. Regressed: upload.filename is stored unchanged as FileUpload.name

sinks.note: the repo's own example app registers handle_upload as the ui.upload on_upload handler (top-level code, not in the slice); it builds video_path = DATA_DIR / args.file.name and calls video_path.write_bytes(...), so a filename such as '../main.py' or an absolute path writes outside DATA_DIR

notes: Recovered fix commit (the advisory links none): f88924c6 is a single-parent 'Merge commit from fork' whose parent f1f75335 is the regressed commit; the regression diff touches only create_file_upload in nicegui/elements/upload_files.py (plus the PurePosixPath import). Class: path-traversal (CWE-22), confirmed by the code: the client-controlled multipart filename flows unchanged into FileUpload.name. The advisory's sink is application code (UPLOAD_DIR / e.file.name); nicegui's own FileUpload.save accepts any path by design and receives no tainted value inside the library. The in-repo demonstration of the flow is examples/ffmpeg_extract_images/main.py::handle_upload (DATA_DIR / args.file.name, then write_bytes), which is the only place in the repository at the regressed commit that joins an uploaded file's name into a filesystem path; examples/ is part of the repo but outside the library package and outside the 2.1 LOC measure. Hops: Upload.__init__ (upload_route closure, request.form) -> create_file_upload (guard) -> Upload.handle_uploads -> events.handle_event -> handler(args) -> handle_upload -> Path.write_bytes. The handler binding (ui.upload(..., on_upload=handle_upload)) is a top-level statement inside a 'with' block in the example and cannot be kept by the slicer; the callback edge is therefore implicit in the slice, and the example globals results and upload (assigned in that block) and the DATA_DIR.mkdir call appear as free names / are absent in the sliced example (the dropped-references check does not see names bound inside a with block). Known-incomplete fix: PurePosixPath(...).name does not split on backslashes, so on Windows '..\..\x' still escapes; that was fixed separately by d38a702e (GHSA-w8wv-vfpc-hw2w / CVE-2026-39844, 3.10.0) and is not part of this event. The modelled flow ('/'-separated traversal and absolute POSIX paths) is closed by the clean commit. The example also runs ffmpeg via subprocess with video_path as a list argument (no shell); that is not an injection flow and is not modelled.
